neighbours.label: ' a' after 'on', in a time or place phrase (on a cold day, on a busy street, on a Friday)
fire: Most shops here shut early on a public holiday.
The old couple met on a train to Vienna.
Nobody plans a picnic on a stormy afternoon.
My office is on a narrow lane by the river.
The match was played on a wet evening in June.
He proposed on a Tuesday, of all days.
Sailors spent years on a whaling ship.
The cafe stands on a corner near the bank.
quiet: Most shops here shut early on the eve of the holiday.
The old couple met in Vienna on the way home.
Nobody plans a picnic in the rain.
My office is by the river near the old mill.
The match was played last June in the mud.
He proposed at noon, of all times.
Sailors spent years at sea with no pay.
The cafe stands near the bank in town.

short: ' a' after on (retest with varied sentences)
notes: Second round, a deliberate retest. The first round held but used a few templates, and varied probes stayed at 0.13-0.28, so I expect this to fail.
